notes: PH/TR/AE/VN current-fact reconciliation: Globe tourist 30-day hard cap; Turkey legacy 90-day YKN cap repealed in 2026; du Tourist SIM 90-day + documented AED5 extension; Viettel VTVANG 50,000 VND/12mo specialist-reported with foreign-acquisition/KYC constraints.

routes.acquisitionSummary: Current Globe prepaid terms still contain a one-year regular-load rule for ordinary registered prepaid lines, but foreign nationals registered as tourists are a separate case: their SIM/eSIM automatically expires 30 days after registration. The old cheap yearly-keep framing therefore does not apply to the target foreign-tourist route.

keep.action: Foreign-tourist registration is the binding rule for this use case: Globe states the tourist SIM/eSIM automatically expires 30 days after registration. The ordinary one-year regular-load rule is not an annual keep path for a tourist-registered line.

routes.chinaActivation: Foreign tourists must register the SIM with passport bio page, current visa stamp, proof of Philippine address and a return/onward ticket. Tourist registration is short-lived rather than a China-first long-term retention route.
routes.kyc: SIM registration is mandatory. Globe states foreign tourists need passport, current visa stamp, Philippine address proof and return/onward ticket; tourist SIM registration expires after 30 days.
routes.payment: GlobeOne and GCash support reloads while abroad, but payment convenience does not override the 30-day tourist-registration lifetime.
routes.wifiCalling: Not relied on for this route decision.
routes.roamingSms: Official Globe prepaid roaming support says a prepaid line can keep roaming signal with zero load and can receive incoming texts for free while abroad.
routes.refund: Globe terms state load on a permanently disconnected SIM is not refundable for cash.
routes.holdReason: Foreign-tourist SIM/eSIM registration automatically expires after 30 days, so the legacy one-top-up-per-year framing is not valid for the target overseas foreign-user retention job.
routes.tariffSummary: Tourist registration: 30-day automatic expiry. Ordinary prepaid one-year load rule exists but is not a tourist keep-number path.
guideSteps: HOLD for foreign-tourist long-term retention: registration expires after 30 days.
Do not model the ordinary one-year load rule as a tourist annual keep cost.

routes.acquisitionSummary: The legacy fixed 90-day passport/YKN blocker is stale. BTK Decision 2026/IK-THD/125 removed the old technical clauses that forced passport-registered foreign lines into the 90-day YKN-conversion shutdown path, effective 25 June 2026. Turkcell now offers a current Tourist SIM/eSIM flow using passport identity checks and Türkiye-arrival activation.

keep.action: Do not use the historical 90-day passport cap as the current retention rule. That technical rule was repealed in 2026; a current long-term Tourist-SIM inactivity/number-retention rule has not been established in this packet.

routes.chinaActivation: Application can start online, but Turkcell states the Tourist line becomes usable after arrival in Türkiye. App self-activation for eSIM requires an eSIM/NFC phone, biometric passport scan, NFC passport read, liveness check and video contract confirmation.
routes.kyc: Current Tourist flow accepts a valid passport; in-app activation requires a biometric passport. Türkiye strengthened electronic/biometric subscriber identity rules in 2026, while the old fixed 90-day YKN conversion clause was removed.
routes.payment: Current Tourist application accepts debit/credit cards supporting international and online transactions.
routes.wifiCalling: Not relied on for this route decision.
routes.roamingSms: Current Turkcell Tourist package page says the package is valid only in Türkiye; this packet does not establish reliable overseas incoming OTP/SMS after departure.
routes.refund: Turkcell states Tourist SIM refunds go back to the same credit card after cancellation through customer service.
routes.holdReason: The old 90-day passport blocker is no longer current, but the route still lacks a verified long-term retention rule and overseas incoming-SMS path; activation/use is Türkiye-centered.
routes.tariffSummary: Legacy 90-day YKN blocker repealed in 2026; current Tourist SIM supports passport-based online application/eSIM flow, but long-term retention and overseas OTP remain unverified.
guideSteps: HOLD: do not repeat the pre-June-2026 fixed 90-day passport-cap claim.
Treat as Türkiye tourist connectivity until current long-term retention and overseas OTP evidence exists.

routes.acquisitionSummary: Current du Tourist SIM material establishes a 90-day visitor-line validity. du support also documents an AED5 renewal/extension action during the 90-day validity, while current tourist eSIM bundles are positioned as short-stay products. This is not evidence of indefinite annual retention.

keep.action: Tourist SIM is valid for 90 days. du support documents an AED5 renewal/extension action during that validity; current evidence does not establish an indefinitely repeatable one-year keep-number path.

routes.chinaActivation: This is a UAE visitor product. Current du pages support tourist SIM/eSIM purchase and activation, but the identity flow is tied to valid UAE tourist/transit documentation rather than a location-independent long-term number product.
routes.kyc: Tourist customers require valid tourist or transit visa documentation; resident/expatriate prepaid identity paths use Emirates ID or employment/residence documentation.
routes.payment: Current Tourist eSIM purchase is digital; ordinary prepaid recharge/app payment is available.
routes.wifiCalling: Not relied on for this route decision.
routes.roamingSms: du states international roaming can be activated for the Tourist plan; this packet does not establish free or reliable incoming OTP SMS abroad.
routes.refund: Not relied on for this route decision.
routes.holdReason: The documented product is a short-term Tourist SIM with 90-day validity and an extension path, not a verified indefinite low-cost retention product; long-term overseas OTP evidence is missing.
routes.tariffSummary: Tourist SIM: 90-day validity; official support documents AED5 renewal/extension; no verified annual/indefinite keep path.
guideSteps: Do not extrapolate a documented 90-day extension into indefinite annual survival.

routes.acquisitionSummary: Recent Viettel-specialist reporting dated February 2026 describes VTVANG as a 12-month keep-number service for eligible prepaid lines. The same current report gives a 50,000 VND registration fee. A first-party Viettel product page for VTVANG was not located in this review, so the keep product remains specialist-reported rather than provider-official.

keep.action: Recent February-2026 Viettel-specialist evidence reports VTVANG at 50,000 VND for 12 months of number retention without normal recharge/activity; eligibility exclusions apply.

routes.chinaActivation: Viettel requires real-name subscriber verification. Current first-party 2026 guidance shows unverified subscribers can have outgoing calls/SMS blocked and overseas subscribers may need My Viettel/Tammi identity remediation. A reliable foreigner-acquisition path is not established here.
routes.kyc: Mandatory subscriber identity verification. Current 2026 Viettel notice emphasizes chip-ID/VNeID-based remediation for affected subscribers; foreign-user onboarding eligibility is not established by first-party evidence in this packet.
routes.payment: VTVANG is reported as an account/SMS service for eligible prepaid lines; foreign payment/onboarding is not established.
routes.wifiCalling: Not relied on for this route decision.
routes.roamingSms: Current Viettel guidance for subscribers abroad states roaming must be active to receive OTP, supporting inbound SMS capability when roaming is active; independent long-term OTP reliability is still unverified.
routes.holdReason: The 50,000 VND/12-month keep package is current specialist evidence but lacks a located first-party product page, and foreign-user acquisition/KYC plus long-term OTP reliability remain unresolved.
routes.tariffSummary: VTVANG reported at 50,000 VND/12 months for eligible prepaid lines; keep as HOLD until first-party product/eligibility and foreign acquisition are verified.
guideSteps: HOLD: treat 50,000 VND/12-month VTVANG as current specialist evidence, not provider-official fact.
Require first-party package/eligibility and foreign-acquisition verification before promotion.
